Subject: Request: Merge accelerator credits across two projects

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — really useful. Quick ask from our side: Novaforge was accepted into two accelerator tracks earlier this year and both project accounts were issued the standard $10,000 trial credits (Account IDs: NF-A-1002 and NF-A-1009). Our engineering work is split across both projects but usage is concentrated in one environment.

Can Redwood make a one-time exception to either:
- consolidate the two credit pools into a single account, or
- allow a transfer of unused credits from NF-A-1009 to NF-A-1002, or
- convert the total unused credits into a committed-reserved credit that we can apply toward a Reserved capacity purchase (we could sign an invoice/PO if needed).

If consolidation is possible we would also like a 6-month extension on the existing expiry dates (they currently expire Oct 1). I attached our internal credit-merge request form for your ops team.

We appreciate any flexibility — this will help us onboard faster and run more realistic load tests. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,

Hi Ava — thanks for the note and the form, got it. Short answer: we can usually only move credits within the same account, but we do offer a few one-time exceptions for accelerator partners in special cases.

Options I can scope right away:
1) Consolidation into a single sandbox/pool under one account (requires Ops sign-off and a quick addendum).
2) Convert unused credits to a Reserved-capacity credit (we issue an invoice for the converted amount; conversion value will be lower than face value and requires finance approval).
3) Limited extension of expiry (we typically do 3–6 months for accelerators on a case-by-case basis).

I've looped in Laura from Customer Ops and Ben from Finance to evaluate the operational and accounting side — they may ask for the account IDs, consumption history, and a signed addendum/PO if we proceed. I attached a draft addendum we typically use as a starting point.

Next steps from my side: 1) Ops/Finance confirm feasibility and proposed conversion math, 2) we send a clean addendum for signature, 3) Ops executes the credit map change.

If either consolidation or conversion is acceptable to you, reply with the preferred path and confirm both account IDs and whether your legal/finance can sign a short addendum + PO within 10 business days.

Cheers,

Laura / Logan —

Finance perspective: consolidation raises revenue recognition and audit trail concerns if credits are moved between account IDs after issuance. To keep accounting clean we recommend the following path as our default: convert the face-value pool of unused credits to a Reserved-capacity credit at a conversion rate (example below) and invoice the converted value. This turns the credit into a contracted instrument and avoids moving issued promotional dollars between ledgers.

Proposed conversion terms (example):
- Face-value pool: $20,000 total (two $10k grants)
- Conversion factor: 70% of face value -> converted credit = $14,000
- Admin fee: one-time $500 processing fee (covers contract amendment and bookkeeping)
- Result: invoice for $13,500 (converted credit less admin fee) which the customer pays and we apply as a Reserved credit balance toward a committed purchase.

Notes:
- If customer declines conversion and only wants consolidation, we will allow a one-time consolidation but document the event in an addendum and leave the original promo allocation visible in the accounting system (i.e., we will not move revenue lines; Ops will map usage to the consolidated account for product purposes).
- Conversion requires a PO and a signed addendum; consolidation requires a signed addendum and ops ticket only.

I recommend we give the customer 30 calendar days to accept the conversion offer to simplify closeout. Happy to run the exact numbers if Ava shares the current unused balances.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Hi Ava — quick follow-up with proposed paths so you have everything in one place.

Option A — Consolidation (one-time):
- We consolidate unused balances from NF-A-1009 into NF-A-1002.
- Requires: confirmation both accounts are Novaforge-owned, signed 1-page addendum, ops ticket (ETA 3 business days after sign).
- Expiry: we can extend both grants up to +6 months from current expiry date.
- Accounting treatment: original promo lines remain in the ledger; Ops will map consumption to NF-A-1002 for product purposes.

Option B — Conversion to Reserved credit (recommended for accounting simplicity):
- We convert the $20,000 face-value pooled credit to a Reserved credit at ~70% conversion (example converted value $14,000).
- Requires PO + signed addendum + $500 admin fee. We issue an invoice for the converted amount less admin fee (example invoice $13,500).
- Conversion results in committed credit that can be applied to Reserved capacity purchases and simplifies revenue recognition.

Next steps if you want to move forward:
1) Confirm which option you prefer.
2) Confirm ownership: NF-A-1002 and NF-A-1009 are under Novaforge AI (reply with the billing/legal entity).
3) If conversion chosen, confirm you can supply a PO within 10 business days and we will prepare the invoice + addendum.

I've attached the addendum draft for review. If you want, we can set a 20-minute alignment call this week to walk through the conversion math live.
